sentences.text: In Canada, nobody votes for the prime minister, or the King.
Who can vote? Canadian citizens from 18, even abroad, and you can register at the polls.
Your ballot lists only your local candidates. Mark the circle next to one.
The most votes wins the riding, even without half.
Each riding's winner joins the House of Commons, which makes the laws and controls the money.
The leader the House backs becomes prime minister. 172 seats is a majority.
The 105 senators aren't elected. The prime minister picks them, to review every law.
The head of state is King Charles. The Governor General stands in for him and signs the laws.
In 2025, Mark Carney's Liberals won 169 seats, three short of a majority.
Then five MPs switched to them, and by-elections did the rest: a majority, with no new election.
Should an MP who switches parties have to face the voters again?
